entries.knownHazards: The plant contains tremetol, a complex alcohol, and glycosides. These toxins cause a fatal disease known as 'staggers' in cattle. The toxin can be passed through the milk and has caused fatalities in humans who have drunk affected cow's milk[274].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Augalas turi tremetolį (sudėtingą alkoholį) ir glikozidus, kurie galvijams sukelia mirtinai pavojingą ligą. Toksinai patenka į pieną ir yra užregistruotų mirties atvejų žmonėms, išgėrusiems užkrėsto karvės pieno.

entries.knownHazards: Euphorbia abyssinica has toxic milky sap that causes irritation and blistering if it comes into contact with the skin. The sap can also cause temporary or permanent blindness if it comes into contact with the eyes.
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Pieniška sula dirgina odą ir sukelia pūsles. Patekusi į akis, gali sukelti laikiną arba nuolatinį aklumą.

entries.knownHazards: The sap contains a latex which is toxic on ingestion and highly irritant externally, causing photosensitive skin reactions and severe inflammation, especially on contact with eyes or open cuts. The toxicity can remain high even in dried plant material[200]. Prolonged and regular contact with the sap is inadvisable because of its carcinogenic nature[214].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Sula turi latekso — toksiškas prarijus, išoriškai sukelia fotodermatitą ir stiprų uždegimą, ypač patekęs į akis ar žaizdas; toksiškumas išlieka ir džiovintoje medžiagoje. Ilgalaikis sąlytis nerekomenduojamas dėl kancerogeninių savybių.

entries.knownHazards: Large quantities of the raw seed may be toxic[159].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Dideli kiekiai žalių sėklų gali būti toksiški.

entries.knownHazards: Although no specific mention has been seen for this species, large quantities of the seed of many species in this genus are thought to be toxic.

entries.knownHazards: Large quantities of the seed may be toxic[65, 76].

entries.knownHazards: Although no specific mention has been made for this species, there have been reports that some members of this genus can cause photosensitivity in susceptible people. Many species also contain oxalic acid (the distinctive lemony flavour of sorrel) - whilst not toxic this substance can bind up other minerals making them unavailable to the body and leading to mineral deficiency. Having said that, a number of common foods such as sorrel and rhubarb contain oxalic acid and the leaves of most members of this genus are nutritious and beneficial to eat in moderate quantities. Cooking the leaves will reduce their content of oxalic acid. entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Lapai turi oksalatų, kurie gali trukdyti mineralų įsisavinimui; sergantieji reumatu, podagra, inkstų akmenligė ar hiperacidumu turėtų vengti. Kai kuriais atvejais gali sukelti fotojautrumą — lapus verdant oksalatų kiekis mažėja.

entries.knownHazards: Avoid for asthmatics. Use by children for diarhoea not recommended or for children under 12 due to salicylate content (risk of Reye's syndrome) [301].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Astmatikams vartoti nerekomenduojama. Dėl salicilatų kiekio neduoti vaikams iki 12 metų (Reye sindromo rizika).

entries.knownHazards: Leaves contain the glycoside Phillyrin[179], its potency is unknown.
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Lapai turi glikozidą filyriną; jo toksiškumas žmonėms nenustatytas.

entries.knownHazards: Poisonous to ruminants[76], it has also caused dermatitis in some people[76].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Toksiškas atrajotojams. Kai kuriems žmonėms gali sukelti dermatitą.

entries.knownHazards: Contact with the sap has caused skin or systemic allergic reactions in some people[238].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Sąlytis su sula gali sukelti odos ar sisteminę alerginę reakciją.

entries.knownHazards: The stem is clothed with brown hairs which rub off easily and can be a severe irritant[166]. When pruning it is best to wear a mask[166]. The eyes can be badly affected[202].

entries.knownHazards: Agave cantala is a species in the genus Agave which contains approximately 257 to 341 species and belongs to the family of the Agavaceae (Century-plant Family). The type species of the genus is Agave americana.
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Nėra duomenų apie žinomus pavojus.

entries.knownHazards: The leaves are used as a fish poison[348 ]. This is probably due to a high content of saponins in the leaves[K ].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Lapai naudojami kaip žuvų nuodai dėl didelio saponinų kiekio.

entries.knownHazards: A few reports exist, none of them in Britain, of toxicity to mammals[76], though the plant is often fed to cows and goats in order to increase their milk yield[238].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Yra keletas pranešimų apie toksiškumą žinduoliams (ne Britanijoje), nors augalas plačiai naudojamas karvių ir ožkų primilžiui didinti.

entries.knownHazards: One report says that the fruit is poisonous[200]. This is somewhat surprising in what is normally seen as a toxin-free genus.
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Vienas šaltinis nurodo, kad uogos toksiškos, tačiau ši žinia yra netikėta, nes giminė paprastai laikoma saugia.

entries.knownHazards: The pure distilled essential oil is toxic in large doses[222]. If used orally may aggravate stomach ulcers. Do not use if allergic to aspirin. Avoid if under 12. Topical use can cause contact dermatitis [301].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Grynas eterinis aliejus didelėmis dozėmis toksiškas; gali paūminti skrandžio opą ir nerekomenduojamas alergiškiems aspirinui bei vaikams iki 12 metų. Išorinis naudojimas gali sukelti kontaktinį dermatitą.

entries.knownHazards: All parts of the plant usually contain toxic alkaloids[200]. Eating just one flower has reportedly been lethal to children[207, 222]. The plant can also cause skin allergies in some people and it is possible that the plant toxins can be absorbed through the skin, especially if there are cuts[238].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Visi augalo dalys turi toksiškų alkaloidų — vienas žiedas gali būti mirtinas vaikui. Toksinai gali prasiskverbti pro odą, ypač per žaizdas.
